name: bioenergetic_internalization
description: A reusable bioenergetic-internalization module (Module H). An evolutionary control loop (replicator dynamics, Sojo-2014 leaky-membrane fitness) under a declining external gradient: as the geochemical pmf collapses, an efficient-pump population internalizes gradient generation and persists, while a weak-pump control collapses (the Sojo constraint). catalyst_efficiency sets the arm. Coarse-grained, deterministic reproduction (not wrapped ALife).

gradient_floor.description: Floor the external gradient decays to (V); low floor forces internalization-or-die

decline.doc:
Ramps the external geochemical gradient down over the run — the environment
the lineages must adapt to. Writes a linearly declining electric potential from
``v_start`` toward ``v_floor``; the selection loop reads it and (if its pump is
efficient enough) internalizes before the gradient collapses.

_contract.summary: Linearly declining external electric potential — the environmental gradient the bioenergetic-selection loop must adapt to.
_contract.description: Writes electric_potential = max(v_floor, v_start - decline_rate * t), the lowering geochemical gradient that drives selection toward internalized gradient generation.
assumptions: Monotone linear decline (a controlled environmental sweep, not a scripted upgrade of the cells).

selection.doc:
Deterministic replicator-dynamics evolutionary control loop over membrane
strategies (permeability × active-pump rate), with a Sojo-2014 leaky-membrane
fitness. Reads the external gradient (electric potential) and catalyst
efficiency; selects strategies ∝ free-energy flux each generation; and emits
the population's lineage fitness, free-energy flux, internalization fraction
and mean permeability (overwrite sensors — the current population state).

_contract.summary: Evolutionary control loop (replicator dynamics) over membrane strategies with Sojo-2014 leaky-membrane fitness: does selection internalize gradient generation as the external gradient drops?
_contract.description: Coarse-grained, deterministic selection model (the study's proposed primary method; not a wrapped ALife/MD engine). A grid of membrane strategies (permeability P × active-pump rate) competes for free-energy flux = k_ext*external_pmf*P + k_int*pump*efficiency*(1-P) - c_pump*pump - c_base. Replicator dynamics select strategies proportional to flux each generation; as the external gradient is lowered the population internalizes (mass shifts to tight-membrane, high-pump strategies) only where the pump beats its cost against the lost external coupling — the Sojo leaky-membrane constraint. All outputs are overwrite sensors; the population is integrated internally.

inputs.electric_potential: external geochemical gradient available to tap (volt)

outputs.internalization: mean active-pump fraction of the surviving population (dimensionless, 0-1)
outputs.survivors: fraction of strategy mass above the survival threshold (dimensionless)

assumptions: Coarse-grained deterministic replicator dynamics (reproducible); the proposed primary method.
Sojo-2014 fitness: tapping the external gradient needs leak (∝ P); internal pumping needs a tight membrane (∝ 1-P) and pays a cost.
Internalization is an evolutionary outcome, not a scripted upgrade.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
